propositions: Completion close (verify → sign) reads HEAD independently at verify and sign steps, allowing unrelated commits to land between them and split the attestation from verification

When HEAD drifts between verify and sign, rebar refuses to sign the stale tree but closes the ticket anyway without a completion attestation, leaving it in a permanently unsigned state with no recovery
The suggested recovery (re-close to certify) is a no-op because the ticket is already closed, and only --force-close or manifest fabrication are available as workarounds
Default path (no --ref) still reads HEAD twice and is vulnerable to TOCTOU; the --ref path from 80af only fixed explicit-ref cases

Completion close should either pin one revision for the entire verify+sign+close unit (so concurrent commits cannot split attestation from verification) or abort without closing when drift is detected, leaving the ticket retryable
